title: Astrophysical Graviton Squeezing Can Be Hidden in the Far-Field
authors: Cheng-Jun Fang, Zong-Kuan Guo, Zhen-Hong Lyu, Jing Shu, Yu-Heng Sun, Zi-Zheng Zhou
abstract: While localized astrophysical sources can generate macroscopic graviton squeezing, their observable quantum signatures at far-field detectors remain unresolved. In this work, we investigate the propagation dynamics of the squeezed states using spatial quantum optics methods to evaluate correlation functions accessible to a local observer. Crucially, we reveal a severe kinematic conflict in same-cone measurements, which highly suppresses local quantum coherence. Consequently, these macroscopically squeezed states appear classically thermal to a single detector. Our results demonstrate that global squeezing does not guarantee local observability, and the measurable quantum signatures may be significantly weaker than what would be expected from the overall squeezing parameter of the state.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the observability of quantum squeezing in astrophysical gravitational waves at a distant detector. It finds that due to kinematic conflicts in same-cone measurements, the expected quantum signatures are severely suppressed, causing the signal to appear classically thermal. This demonstrates a crucial limitation: global quantum properties do not automatically translate into local, measurable quantum effects.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the global quantum squeezing of gravitons, generated by astrophysical sources, can manifest as measurable local quantum coherence at a far-field detector.
main_result: A severe kinematic conflict in same-cone measurements causes local quantum coherence to be highly suppressed, meaning global squeezing does not guarantee local observability; the signal appears effectively classical/thermal.
method: The analysis employs spatial quantum optics methods, calculating two-time correlation functions ($g^{(2)}$) and analyzing the far-field expansion of the graviton field using pole extraction techniques.
model_or_system: The system involves gravitons (gravitational waves) propagating from localized astrophysical sources to a far-field detector. The state is modeled as a multi-mode squeezed state, analyzed via an Effective Field Theory (EFT) Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Second-order correlation function ($g^{(2)}$), local quantum coherence, and the anomalous moment ($M_D$) relative to the normal moment ($N_D$).
important_parameters: The suppression factor $\eta \sim \exp(-dE/k^*)$, the far-field distance $r$, and the angular separation $\delta	heta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the far-field limit ($r \gg L_D$) and relies on the detector sampling only a single far-field line of sight (same-cone measurement).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the far-field projection onto the outgoing branch ($I_+$) and compare overlap integrals for normal and anomalous moments, highlighting the kinematic conflict.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the far-field expansion of the field (pole extraction), then calculating the relevant correlation functions ($g^{(2)}$) using overlap integrals, and finally demonstrating the exponential suppression factor arising from the same-cone measurement geometry.
why_interesting: The core mechanism of suppression—where geometric constraints (like single-line-of-sight detection) destroy quantum correlations—is a powerful concept applicable to any field where global quantum resources are mapped onto local measurements, such as quantum sensing or quantum communication.
